text: Question: Why is there no network coverage in my area? Answer: ### Short Answer Coverage gaps can result from terrain/building obstruction, an outage under investigation, or the area being outside current tower footprint. Check Network > Coverage Map in the app for real-time status, or report the location so our Network team can log it for planning. ### Detailed Explanation The three listed causes are meaningfully different in what a customer can do about them: obstruction is often a fixed physical constraint, an active outage is temporary and being worked on, and being outside the tower footprint is a coverage-planning issue — the coverage map and location-reporting flow exist to help distinguish which of the three applies. ### Key Details | Detail | Value | |---|---| | Where to check | Network > Coverage Map in the app | | Possible causes | Terrain/building obstruction; outage under investigation; outside current tower footprint | | If none apply / for planning | Report the location for the Network team to log | ### Troubleshooting | Symptom | Possible Cause | Diagnostic Check | Recommended Action | |---|---|---|---| | No coverage, area shown covered on map | Terrain/building obstruction, or a temporary outage | Coverage map status vs. Service Status for that area | Check both; if map shows covered but Service Status flags an outage, wait for restoration | | No coverage, area shown outside footprint | Location is outside current tower coverage | Coverage map boundary for the exact location
title: Why is there no network coverage in my area?
